phase: P03 (batch 3: user/admin queries, repositories, profile service, domain entities and value objects)
reviewed_without_change: All /users/:userId and /admin/users routes are ADMIN_ONLY; /users/me and profile/session routes use the token's user id.
User DTOs and the admin listing projection exclude password hash, 2FA secret and Stripe customer id.
Admin listing: search length capped, sortBy whitelisted (createdAt, email), page size capped at 100.
Email and phone value objects validate format and length; status/role transitions emit events and are guarded by the admin safety rules from P07-04.

findings.problem: Profiles are created on the first update. That creation path stored defaultAddressId/defaultPaymentMethodId without the ownership check applied on later updates, so a user could point their profile at another customer's address or payment method (ids only; no other customer's details were returned).
findings.change: Ownership of both references is checked before anything is written, for new and existing profiles.
findings.verification: Unit profile-default-ownership: baseline 2/2 failed (another user's address/payment method accepted on first update); fixed refused with nothing saved.

findings.problem: Date of birth accepted any well-formed date, including future dates.
findings.change: Date of birth must be in the past and on or after 1900.
findings.verification: Boundary tests: future and pre-1900 dates rejected; existing accepted forms unchanged.

tests.new: unit profile-default-ownership (2), validation boundary date-of-birth cases (2)
tests.final: 1487 unit tests in 115 files; all user-management unit, integration and E2E tests (76) on a disposable database; root/tooling tsc; 7/7 workspace type-checks; API client drift check; ESLint and Prettier

p03_status: Batches 1-3 cover authentication, account management, user/admin queries, repositories and domain rules. Open P03 items are infrastructure/owner decisions: the in-memory token store (move to Redis before running more than one API instance), ImageKit upload restrictions, avatar host restriction, admin user hard delete vs deactivate-and-anonymise, and the shared access/refresh token secret.
